summary: A notice from Alex McKenzie at BBN that Vint Cerf's UCLA group would run heavy-traffic performance experiments on the network on May 8, 1972. These could lock up the network so that no traffic flows, a problem the upcoming new IMP software was meant to prevent. Sites were advised not to schedule important network work that day.

plainLanguage.summary: UCLA researchers planned a heavy-traffic test of the network on May 8, 1972. Because the test might stop all traffic, BBN asked sites to avoid scheduling important network work that day.

subtitle: A warning about heavy-traffic network experiments

tldr.problem: Researchers wanted to measure network behavior under heavy traffic directed to one site before new IMP software was installed.
tldr.mechanism: The experiments were scheduled for May 8 and could cause the network to stop carrying traffic.
tldr.outcome: BBN advised sites not to plan important network work for that day.

today: RFC 334 is an operational warning about planned ARPANET performance experiments. It explains the test's purpose and the risk known when the notice was issued.

sections.title: The Planned Network Test
sections.content: Vint Cerf of UCLA's Network Measurement Center requested performance experiments before new IMP software was installed on May 15. The experiments were scheduled for May 8 and would measure network performance when heavy traffic was directed to one site.
sections.plainLanguage: The researchers planned to send a heavy load of traffic toward one site and measure how the network handled it. They scheduled the test before an IMP software installation.

sections.title: Risk of a Network Lockup
sections.content:
The notice says the experiments might cause the network to lock up so that no traffic could flow. The planned new IMP software was designed to prevent this problem, but the test was considered important despite the risk.

BBN says it agreed to assist with the experiments after ARPA indicated their importance.
sections.plainLanguage: The test might stop all network traffic. The new software was intended to prevent that problem, but the researchers still wanted to measure the network before installing it.

sections.title: Advice to Network Sites
sections.content: BBN did not know whether the experiments would cause a lockup. It advised sites not to schedule important network work on Monday, May 8, and apologized for the late announcement.
sections.plainLanguage: Because an outage was possible, BBN asked sites to avoid important network tasks on the test day. The notice also apologized for arriving late.
